conviction_note: Two real, opposing findings that mostly cancel: a company-disclosed but never-aggregated ~85% collapse in the buyback run-rate that tomorrow's 10-Q will make visible (negative, -1.8) against a Q1 revenue setup that is unusually well supported by peer read-across, an easy comp, a full quarter of Reliant and $70m of one-off event revenue, with Q1 margin weakness already pre-guided (positive, +0.8); net -1.0, well inside the 9.8% implied move which is itself unreliable at a 46%-of-mid ATM spread.

findings.finding: Sunbelt's buyback has been throttled by roughly 85%: treasury shares rose only from 3,993,501 (29 May 2026) to 4,699,397 (28 Aug 2026) — 705,896 shares in 13 weeks, ~54k/week or ~$4m/week at prevailing prices, an annualised ~$210m — versus $1,413m of buybacks in FY26 and 405,000 shares in the single week of 6-10 April 2026 under the same $1.5bn programme launched 2 March 2026; shares outstanding are flat at ~409.8m and the weekly notices show the pace decaying monotonically (405k Apr 6-10, 135k Apr 13-17, 75k Apr 27-May 1, 60k May 26-29, 60k Jun 15-18, 43k Jul 6-10, 17k Aug 10-14, 13k Aug 17-21, 23k Aug 24-28, 47k Aug 31-Sep 4).
findings.why_not_priced: The data exists only as LSE/UK-MAR-format 'Transaction in Own Shares' / 'Share Repurchase Program - Weekly Report' notices that no US vendor parses into a time series, and nobody sums them. The coverage that does exist reads each notice as confirmation the programme is running — TipRanks headlines them 'Sunbelt Rentals Continues $1.5 Billion Buyback' and 'Boosts Treasury Stock With Ongoing $1.5 Billion Buyback', and a Simply Wall St narrative still lists 'Cash Returns And Index Support' as a pillar of fair value. If the market had done the arithmetic you would see (a) FY27 EPS estimates cut on the share-count line, because a $1.5bn programme executed on the prior 18-month cadence implies ~20m shares / ~5% of the count retired and the actual count is going nowhere (420.4m weighted diluted FY26, 412.5m in Q4 FY26, ~409.8m outstanding now), (b) the capital-return leg stripped out of bull cases, and (c) the option skew bid for downside rather than -3.35 vol points the other way. Tomorrow's 10-Q Item 5 issuer-purchase table and the diluted share count make the Q1 number explicit for the first time: roughly 250k shares / ~$19m repurchased in a quarter in which the company also closed $650m of Reliant and raised $1.2bn of notes.
findings.independence: A different document points the same way: the FY26 Q4 press release (SEC 8-K exhibit) gives no free cash flow guidance for FY27 at all, while guiding gross rental capex UP to $2.45-2.85bn — Ashtead's practice under the old reporting regime was to give and even raise FCF guidance (it raised FY26 FCF guidance at the Q1 print on 3 Sept 2025). https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002083785/000162828026044797/sunbeltpressrelease-fy26q4.htm and https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/ashtead-q1-fy26-slides-rental-revenue-up-24-raises-free-cash-flow-guidance-93CH-4220646 . The weekly repurchase notices (detail/100, detail/122, detail/137, detail/155, detail/157 and the 2 June 2026 notice) are one source cluster and should be collapsed to one; the treasury-share balances and the per-week share counts inside them are two readings of the same filings, not independent evidence.

findings.finding: The Q1 FY27 (May-July 2026) volume setup is unusually well supported and the margin worry is pre-guided: the comp is +2.4% group rental revenue in Q1 FY26, Q4 FY26 exited at +8.0%, the $650m Reliant/Aries modular business closed 1 May 2026 so the full quarter is inorganically boosted, management flagged ~$70m of Q1-specific FIFA World Cup and UFC event revenue on the June call and said margins improve 'in the back half', and both peers reported record calendar Q2 and RAISED full-year guidance (URI rental revenue +12.7%, fleet productivity +3.4%, FY revenue guide lifted to $17.5-17.8bn from $16.9-17.4bn on 22 July; Herc rental revenue +23%, guidance raised on 28 July).
findings.why_not_priced: The individual inputs are wire copy; what is not is that the baseline's -14.35% 20-day run-in carries essentially zero SUNB-specific information. URI is down 13.2% over the past month from an all-time-high close on 17 Aug and sits at $1,014.46 against a 52-week high of $1,179.18, i.e. -14.0% from its high on the same tape and the same macro (the 4 Sept hot payrolls print lifted rate-hike odds and hit cyclicals). So the run-in is group beta, not the market pre-positioning for a bad Sunbelt quarter. If it were company-specific de-risking you would expect puts to exist — put/call open interest is 0.02 on 16,845 total contracts and the 25-delta skew is -3.35 vol points, so nobody has actually bought downside on this name. The asymmetry is that the sell-side tone into the print is set by JPMorgan's Underweight and $71 target dated 2 Sept, which rests on a margin thesis management already telegraphed as a first-half phenomenon.
findings.independence: Separate source, separate company: United Rentals' own Q2 2026 release (22 July 2026) https://investors.unitedrentals.com/press-releases/press-releases-details/2026/United-Rentals-Announces-Record-Second-Quarter-Results-and-Raises-Full-Year-2026-Guidance/default.aspx and Herc's Q2 2026 release via ARA's Rental Management https://news.ararental.org/herc-reports-q2-2026-results-increases-full-year-guidance ; the URI price/52-week-high anchor is https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/uri/ . These are independent of the Sunbelt transcript and of the buyback filings used in finding 1.

searched_and_found_nothing: S&P 500 index-committee flow: the 4 Sept 2026 S&P DJI announcement added Bloom Energy, Illumina and Everpure effective 21 Sept and did not mention SUNB (https://press.spglobal.com/2026-09-04-Bloom-Energy,-Illumina,-and-Everpure-Set-to-Join-S-P-500-Others-to-Join-S-P-100,-S-P-MidCap-400,-and-S-P-SmallCap-600); SUNB was already down to $67.11 on 3 Sept, i.e. before the announcement, so there is no 'passed-over' trade to harvest and no mechanical inclusion flow contaminating the print window

FTSE UK index deletion flow: the listing transfer and index exit happened in February 2026 (FTSE Russell informative notice 28 Jan 2026, https://research.ftserussell.com/products/index-notices/home/getnotice/?id=2618540) and SUNB is not in the September 2026 FTSE UK quarterly review (https://www.lseg.com/en/media-centre/press-releases/2026/ftse-uk-index-series-review-september-2026) — the mechanical flow the brief worried about is nine months stale
WARN notices, layoffs or branch closures for Sunbelt Rentals in 2026 — nothing found in state WARN databases or news via search
Sunbelt UK / A-Plant disposal or strategic review — no evidence of any process, despite the redomicile making a UK exit an obvious next step
CEO/CFO or senior leadership transition — leadership page and news show no change; nothing pending

Annual meeting of 1 Sept 2026 (8-K item 5.07, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2083785/000119312526380411/d55578d8k.htm): all ten directors elected, say-on-pay approved, annual frequency approved, PwC ratified — no governance dissent worth trading

Form 4 cluster: the 4 Sept 2026 disclosure is routine — 2,354 RSUs at $0.00 to each of nine directors on 1 Sept and small tax-withholding dispositions at $72.28 on 31 Aug; no open-market insider buying or selling

Used-equipment residual values: only calendar-Q1 2026 Ritchie Bros data available (US aerials/telehandlers/forklifts softer on volume, earthmoving firmer) — too stale and too mixed to say anything about the May-July quarter's disposal gains
ARA industry forecast: the August 2026 update (+3.4% US CIE and general tool rental in 2026 to $83.5bn, +4.4% in 2027) is in line with company guidance — no revision to trade
Customer-side signal: Sunbelt is B2B with no consumer app of consequence, so app-store review volume/rating and consumer forum sentiment produced nothing usable

A specific SUNB-only cause for the mid-August-to-September fall: none found beyond the group de-rate and JPMorgan's 2 Sept target cut to $71 — the Wells Fargo Overweight/$96 initiation around 17 Aug in fact marked the local high
baseline_tension: The buyback finding cuts against the baseline's 'upside paid' read (25-delta skew -3.35, put/call OI 0.02) but that read should carry almost no weight — 16,845 total contracts and a 46%-of-mid ATM spread on a seven-month-old US listing means the option market here is a listing-age artifact, not a directional statement, and the same artifact makes the 9.76% implied move an overstatement I am deliberately not sizing to; the read-across finding cuts against the -14.35% run-up by showing it is almost entirely URI-shaped sector beta rather than company-specific pre-print de-risking.
